title: Zambia Catch Up caregiver attendance-information messaging

lifecycle.note: The previously verified substantive evidence is unchanged; this candidate corrects routing clarity, compact provenance, and lifecycle metadata.

user_context.archetype: Zambia education implementer already considering or operating Catch Up
user_context.decision: Whether a caregiver attendance-information messaging add-on should be tested next alongside existing Catch Up, rather than scaled or treated as proven.
user_context.scope: Grade 3-5 Catch Up pupils where child-level school/Catch Up exposure is measurable and targeted caregivers plausibly have a material, actionable information gap about that exposure.

feasible_options.label: TEST
feasible_options.description: Run a small randomized, information-gap-targeted add-on pilot of weekly caregiver information on school and Catch Up attendance.

feasible_options.label: DO NOT TEST
feasible_options.description: Do not run the messaging pilot when caregivers already know the relevant exposure state, messages cannot reliably reach them, or the bottleneck is not family-controllable.

feasible_options.label: CANNOT DECIDE
feasible_options.description: Use when local exposure-data capability, caregiver information-gap/deliverability, or incremental pilot cost cannot be established well enough to route the decision.

routing_recommendation.current_route_reason: The canonical repository does not yet contain the required Zambia operational observations establishing reconstructable exposure states, a material/actionable caregiver information gap, reliable message delivery/comprehension, a family-controllable bottleneck, and pilot micro-costing. Therefore TEST is not the present-tense recommendation.
routing_recommendation.rule: Move from CANNOT DECIDE to TEST only if reliable child-level data can cheaply distinguish school absence, present-but-missed Catch Up, Catch Up non-delivery, and Catch Up attendance; a bounded pre-pilot check shows targeted caregivers have a material, actionable information gap about those states; messages can be received/understood reliably enough; the missed exposure is plausibly family-controllable; and pilot micro-costing is acceptable. If a required observation is merely missing, remain CANNOT DECIDE. If a gate is observed to fail, route DO NOT TEST.
not_authorized: claim of superior cost-effectiveness versus standard Catch Up

closest_same_package_research.setting: seven low-income schools in Santiago, Chile
closest_same_package_research.intervention: weekly attendance messages plus monthly grade/behavior messages
closest_same_package_research.attendance_effect: +1.1 percentage points average; attendance response concentrated among students at higher dropout risk rather than low-risk students
closest_same_package_research.use: research denominator only; not a Zambia budget estimate

mechanism_close_african_evidence.result: weekly parent messages reporting after-school-program attendance increased attendance about 5.6%-6.1%
mechanism_close_african_evidence.reported_cost: about R1.01 per child per week
mechanism_close_african_evidence.limitation: no downstream learning outcome; accounting scope is not portable to Zambia

zambia_local_feasibility_evidence.intervention: nine-month parent-facing SMS plus monthly-meeting early-reading package
zambia_local_feasibility_evidence.limitation: different bundled intervention; does not isolate attendance/exposure and is not a cost denominator for attendance messaging

required_zambia_denominators: incremental cost per additional realized Catch Up session
benefits_costs_denominators.cannot_compare: Current evidence cannot defensibly compare caregiver messaging cost-effectiveness with standard Catch Up or other marginal interventions because denominators, packages, settings, and mechanisms are incompatible.

uncertainties_and_contrary_evidence: The closest cost+attendance+learning evidence is from Chile, not Zambia.
The closest same-package attendance effect was heterogeneous, concentrated among students at higher dropout risk, so a broad untargeted effect should not be assumed.
Message receipt in the closest-source review was only about 60%, making deliverability a causal implementation gate rather than a minor operational detail.
Cape Town evidence is mechanism-close but lacks learning outcomes and comes from a master's thesis.
The Zambia SMS evidence changes home reading directly and includes monthly meetings, so it does not identify attendance messaging as the causal mechanism.
Messaging cannot fix Catch Up non-delivery or other non-family-controllable causes of missed exposure.
An attendance gain has limited decision value if it does not increase realized Catch Up sessions or if added exposure does not improve policy-relevant learning.
adoption_constraints: reliable Catch Up session delivery and attendance data
evidence that targeted caregivers have a material, actionable information gap about recent child/Catch Up exposure
caregiver phone-number matching and sufficiently reliable message receipt
message comprehension and a plausible caregiver action in response
SIM churn, language, and caregiver literacy
low incremental data-cleaning and staff burden
adequate Catch Up instructional quality when sessions are attended

toward_do_not_test: caregivers already know the relevant attendance/exposure state
reliable message receipt is too low
information is not understandable or actionable
exposure states cannot be distinguished cheaply
pilot micro-costing is high relative to plausible exposure gain
messaging cannot target a family-controllable bottleneck
toward_test: the four exposure states are reliably reconstructable
targeted caregivers demonstrably have a material/actionable information gap
messages are reliably received and understood
toward_scale_later: randomized Zambia evidence in the relevant target population shows meaningful added realized Catch Up exposure
incremental cost per added session is decision-competitive using compatible denominators
effects persist and implementation/message receipt remain reliable
stop_after_pilot: caregiver knowledge does not change where an information gap was expected
recorded attendance rises without meaningful added Catch Up exposure
added exposure does not improve policy-relevant learning

highest_value_next_information_request: Before committing to the pilot, obtain a small Zambia Catch Up operational sample that jointly measures whether the four exposure states can be reconstructed reliably, whether intended caregivers have a material/actionable information gap about those states and can reliably receive/understand messages, and the micro-cost of producing those states and sending/monitoring weekly messages.
